implementation_notes: tower-sessions supplies the classic roles as tower middleware: SessionManagerLayer owns creation, validation and expiry, and a SessionStore implementation owns persistence (MemoryStore in-process; Redis, SQLx, MongoDB, sled and others for shared state). Handlers receive a Session extractor with get/insert/remove/flush, and expiry is declared with Expiry::OnInactivity or Expiry::OnSessionEnd. Stores without server-side TTL need the continuously_delete_expired task. actix-session is the equivalent for actix-web; the architecture is the same, so the choice is ecosystem, not idiom.
pitfalls: Sessions are loaded lazily only in handlers that use the Session extractor, so a request that never touches the session does not refresh an inactivity expiry.
MemoryStore is per-process and volatile; production multi-instance deployments need a persistent SessionStore plus its expiry strategy.
Stores without built-in TTL (SQLx, MongoDB) silently accumulate expired rows unless continuously_delete_expired is spawned.
Session values must be serde-serializable; changing the stored shape breaks old sessions unless the value type tolerates it.
